editorial.headline: The Office Behind the Office
editorial.standfirst: This contract-based administrative service is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but a Bali-wide PMA moratorium makes registration unavailable on the island today.
editorial.body:
At its core, KBLI 82100 is the outsourced office function: the everyday administrative work a business asks another party to perform for a fee or under contract. That can mean reception, financial planning, billing and recordkeeping, personnel administration, and mail services. It is not merely a back-office label. The scope reaches from document preparation—editing, final checking, typing, word processing and pre-filing—to transcription, letter or résumé writing, duplication, blueprint production, and self-service photocopy operations.

Its practical centre is useful order: supporting secretarial work, rented post-office boxes, postal and mailing services such as pre-sorting and addressing, file digitisation without subsequent data processing, and e-book formatting. The activity is designed for service providers acting for other parties, rather than for a company simply handling its own internal administration. The permitted scale is broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar are all open. That makes it a classification suited to an administrative-service business from its smallest operating form through to a large enterprise.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The activity is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. For a foreign investor considering Indonesian registration outside Bali, the record therefore permits a fully foreign-owned structure, subject to the classification as stated. The national position should not be diluted by assumptions drawn from the nature of office work: the record’s stated ceiling is complete foreign ownership, and its cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Yet Bali calls for the opposite conclusion today. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope, and the Bali moratorium blocks it on that basis. The provincial rule is island-wide and permanent: it blocks PMA registration for activities classified Low or Medium-Low risk. This is not a reduction of the national 100% ceiling; it is a Bali registration block, effective under the moratorium from May 2026. For founders, the distinction is decisive: national openness does not create a Bali PMA registration route for this activity.

byTheNumbers.value: Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)
